policy_name: Enforce Least Privilege on Service Accounts (Prohibit Primitive Roles)
description: Service accounts must not be granted primitive roles (roles/owner, roles/editor) across projects or organizations.
rationale: Primitive roles grant blanket data access and administrative mutation rights, violating the principle of least privilege.

policy_name: Enforce 90-Day Cryptographic Rotation for User-Managed Service Account Keys
description: User-managed service account keys must be cryptographically rotated every 90 days or migrated to Workload Identity.
rationale: Stale service account keys pose a major credential leakage risk if committed to version control or local machines.

policy_name: Restrict Unrestricted Inbound SSH Access (Port 22) from Public Internet
description: VPC firewall rules must not permit ingress TCP port 22 from source range 0.0.0.0/0. Remote access must route through Google Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) or approved corporate bastion CIDRs.
rationale: Exposing SSH directly to 0.0.0.0/0 invites automated brute-force attacks and zero-day protocol exploits against compute workloads.

policy_name: Prohibit Direct Public External IPv4 Assignment to Compute Engine Instances
description: Internal database, batch worker, and backend VMs must not possess external public IP addresses; outbound connectivity must route via Cloud NAT.
rationale: Public IPs bypass central egress inspection points and directly expose internal compute instances to external threat actors.

policy_name: Prohibit Public Internet Exposure of GKE Master Control Plane Endpoint
description: GKE cluster master authorized networks must not include 0.0.0.0/0 and private endpoint enforcement must be enabled.
rationale: An internet-facing Kubernetes API server is an extreme target for credential theft, remote code execution, and cluster compromise.

policy_name: Enforce GKE Workload Identity on Production Clusters
description: GKE clusters must enable Workload Identity to eliminate the need for pods to mount long-lived service account JSON keys.
rationale: Static keys mounted inside pods can be exfiltrated via container escape or log inspection; Workload Identity issues short-lived tokens.

policy_name: Enforce Cloud Storage Public Access Prevention (Prohibit allUsers / allAuthenticatedUsers)
description: Cloud Storage buckets must enforce Public Access Prevention (PAP=enforced) and contain no IAM bindings granting roles to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers.
rationale: Accidental exposure of sensitive corporate documents or customer PII via misconfigured bucket permissions is a primary data breach vector.

policy_name: Enforce Uniform Bucket-Level Access (Prohibit Fine-Grained Object ACLs and Authenticated URLs)
description: Cloud Storage buckets must enforce Uniform Bucket-Level Access (UBLA=true) to disable legacy object ACLs, prohibit individual objects from exposing authenticated or public URLs (allAuthenticatedUsers / allUsers), and ensure centralized IAM-only governance.
rationale: Object-level ACLs permit individual objects to be shared with allAuthenticatedUsers or allUsers, bypassing bucket-level IAM policies and exposing sensitive files via public or authenticated URLs.

policy_name: Enforce Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) on Sensitive Cloud Storage Buckets
description: Production and audit storage buckets must utilize Cloud KMS Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) rather than default Google-managed keys.
rationale: CMEK ensures the enterprise retains cryptographic sovereign control over data access, enabling cryptographic revocation.

policy_name: Prohibit Public IPv4 Addresses and 0.0.0.0/0 Authorized Networks on Cloud SQL
description: Cloud SQL database instances must not be configured with public IPv4 addresses or authorized networks permitting 0.0.0.0/0. Communication must occur over Private Service Access (PSA).
rationale: Public database endpoints allow direct attacks against database ports (5432/3306), risking credential stuffing and data exfiltration.

policy_name: Enforce Automated Daily Backups and Point-In-Time Recovery on Cloud SQL
description: Cloud SQL instances must have automated daily backups enabled and binary logging configured for point-in-time recovery (PITR).
rationale: Disabling automated backups risks total permanent data loss in the event of ransomware, human operational error, or regional catastrophe.

policy_name: Restrict BigQuery Dataset Access from allAuthenticatedUsers & Public Principals
description: BigQuery dataset ACLs must not grant READER, WRITER, or OWNER roles to allAuthenticatedUsers or allUsers.
rationale: Granting access to allAuthenticatedUsers allows any entity with a valid Google account worldwide to read enterprise data warehouse tables.

policy_name: Restrict Unauthenticated Invocations on Internal Cloud Run Services
description: Internal business microservices deployed on Cloud Run must require authentication (roles/run.invoker restricted to authorized service accounts).
rationale: Unauthenticated endpoints in internal microservice chains allow unauthenticated external actors to trigger backend business logic.

policy_name: Enforce 90-Day Automatic Key Rotation on Cloud KMS CryptoKeys
description: Cloud KMS symmetric encryption keys must have an automated rotation period configured not exceeding 90 days (7776000s).
rationale: Key rotation limits the amount of ciphertext compromised if a specific cryptographic key version is ever leaked or broken.

policy_name: Enforce CMEK and Automatic Rotation on Secret Manager Secrets
description: Production API tokens and database credentials stored in Secret Manager must be encrypted with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys.
rationale: Sensitive secrets must remain protected under enterprise-managed cryptographic keys to satisfy PCI-DSS mandate.

policy_name: Enforce Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) on Sensitive Pub/Sub Topics
description: Production message bus topics transmitting payment or customer events must be encrypted at rest using Cloud KMS CMEK.
rationale: Pub/Sub messages buffered in memory and disk queues must be cryptographically protected under customer control.
